label: Tutorial: Workflows (task scheduler)
description: Steps of the Tutorial button on the Workflows (task scheduler) page (endpoint task_scheduler.admin_panel). A step: target (CSS selector, empty = centred card), title, text (blank line = new paragraph, **bold**, `code`), roles (optional: anonymous, user, member, admin, perm:<key>), demo (rule / bundle: example shown when the target is missing). A step whose target is not on the screen is skipped.

steps.title: Workflows
steps.text:
A **workflow** is a pipeline of admin jobs that runs on its own: data refreshes, backups, Git updates, feeds, quality scores, checks, notifications…

Its **first task** is launched by a date (once, every day / week / month, or a cron expression); the next ones start **after** another task, on success, on failure or always. Each launch is kept with its logs, so you can see what ran, when, and why it failed.

steps.title: List or calendar
steps.text:
**List**: every workflow, its health and its next launch.

**Calendar**: the launches planned and the ones that happened, day by day — plus your notes and reminders. The admin nav (right) leads to the other admin pages.

steps.title: Create a workflow
steps.text:
**New Workflow**: start empty and add tasks.

**Templates**: ready-made workflows (data refresh, backups, Rulesets publication, rule feeds, Git updates…) created in one click with their tasks and links — the first task is **paused** until you check it. Some templates ask their choices first: **Git Sources updates** reuses a Git updater of Manage Git or creates one with the same form.

**Import**: a `.json` exported from this page, here or on another instance.

Each workflow can also be **duplicated**, **exported** or **saved as a template** from its row.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Finds workflows by title, description **and** by the tasks they contain.

steps.title: The workflows
steps.text:
Click a row to open the workflow. Click a column header to sort.

**Tasks** unfolds the tasks with their icons. **Health**: one dot per recent launch (green done, red failed) and the success rate. **Next launch**: when it runs next — *Never runs* means no task can start on its own.

A Git logo next to a title: the workflow runs Git updates (GitHub, GitLab…). The **switch** in Actions pauses / resumes the workflow; the other buttons edit, duplicate, export, save as a template, delete.

steps.title: Cards
steps.text: The same workflows as cards — the Table / Cards switch is kept per browser.

steps.title: Several at once
steps.text: Tick workflows to **stop** their running jobs, **pause** them or **delete** them together. Launching and resuming are done one workflow at a time on purpose.

steps.title: Calendar — schedule by drag and drop
steps.text: Drag a workflow onto a day or an hour to set its launch — the ticked ones come along, spread one after the other. Drag a planned launch to move it. A day has a maximum number of launches (setting `workflows.calendar_max_per_day`). The eye hides a workflow from the calendar.

steps.title: Calendar — what is shown
steps.text: Hide categories when it gets crowded: planned, done, failed, paused launches, notes, reminders. Kept per browser; **Show all** brings everything back.

steps.title: Calendar — days, notes, reminders
steps.text:
**Click a day**: everything on it opens under the calendar (launches, notes, reminders) with Edit / Delete.

The **+** at the bottom right of a day: schedule a workflow, add a **note** (markdown, nothing sent) or a **reminder** — at its date it sends a notification (to you or all admins), an email (to you or addresses you type) or both. Handy for a token that expires.

Click a note or a reminder to read it; drag it to move it.
